structured.response_summary: Squash merging combines all commits from a branch into one new commit on the target branch. It produces a compact, easy-to-scan history, but discards the branch’s individual commit structure and creates a new commit identity. Rebase merging replays each branch commit onto the target branch, preserving separate commits and authorship while rewriting their commit IDs. It retains more development history and supports per-commit reverts or debugging, but can leave a noisier history. Use squash merging when the branch’s intermediate commits are not valuable; use rebase merging when each commit is clean, meaningful, and worth preserving. Both avoid a merge commit and create a linear target-branch history.
